summary: The knowledge (fact) tier and the room-language tier are deleted. Nora loses five tools (search_knowledge, get_knowledge, knowledge_premises, knowledge_asserters, knowledge_entity), the <facts>, <room_language>, <room_exchange> and <room_portrait> prompt blocks, six Dreamer adaptors, and the [facts] and [language] config sections. The note, standing, presence, participation, reminder, event and memory tiers are untouched.
details: Deleted whole: the knowledge tier's adaptors and stores (fact_adaptor, fact_embedder, fact_render, knowledge_search, SqlFactStore, SqlFactCandidateStore, SqlRenderedClaimStore, the shared embedding seam), the language tier's (LanguageConsolidator, LexemeObserver, ExchangeConsolidator, ExchangePatternObserver, PortraitSynthesizer, SqlExchangeStore, SqlRoomPortraitStore and their renderers), the correction loop's Recogniser on the reply path, and seven Dreamer objectives (fact-candidates, fact-adjudication, fact-entity-resolution, fact-dispute, room-language, room-language-verification, room-exchange).

NO MIGRATION DROPS ANY TABLE, deliberately. `fact`, `fact_candidate`, `fact_premise`, `fact_asserter`, `rendered_claim`, `embedding`, `language_observation`, `room_lexeme`, `exchange_observation`, `room_exchange`, `room_portrait` and `dream_schedule_state` all keep their definitions in `nora/infra/sql/schema.py` and their migrations. Dropping them destroys data and is a separate operator decision; the schema-parity gate keeps passing meanwhile.

`fact_entity` and `nora/infra/sql/entities.py` SURVIVE, tier-neutral: `note_entity.entity_id` is a foreign key into that table, and an entity ('Big Walk') is a shared name registry rather than any one tier's property. The store is now built UNCONDITIONALLY at the composition root instead of under `[facts] enabled`. Its `promote()` and `unresolved_names()` — reachable only from the fact tier — are gone, and the literal veto and its operator-owned veto file with them.

The note tier's discharge pipeline loses its `_WorldClaim` branch: it routed a closed note's settled world-facts into the fact store's `propose`, which no longer exists. `_CommitmentClaim` -> the Gathering service and `_PersonClaim` -> Honcho's conclusion lane are unchanged. The note-curation objective no longer asks for a `world_claim`, and one invented anyway is dropped and counted as malformed.

The Dreamer's clock keeps running. Its five numbers (`tick_seconds`, `safety_lag`, `quiet_seconds`, `max_age_seconds`, `batch_limit`) moved from `[language]` to `[dreamer]`, which is where they always belonged: they bound `dream_loop`, which ticks every scheduled adaptor, and a tier flag owning the runtime's clock is what made `[dreamer] enabled = true` inert for five days in August. `[dreamer] model = ""` now falls back to `[llm] model` rather than to `[language] model`.

34 declared metrics went with their recording sites (every `nora_fact_*`, `nora_dispute_*`, `nora_knowledge_*`, `nora_language_*`, `nora_exchange_*`, `nora_rendered_claim_*` and `nora_embedding_store_total` series), and the `fact_candidates.pending` bound site with them.
limitations: THE `fact_entity` REGISTRY NOW HAS NO WRITER. `SqlEntityStore.resolve_or_create` was the mint path and its only production caller was the deleted fact store, which minted an entity for every fact's subject. `SqlNoteStore` reads `resolve` on every note write and deliberately never mints, so with nothing minting, every note anchor resolves to nothing, `note_entity` stays empty, and the note tier's entity-resolution pass sees a near-miss queue with no existing rows to merge into. The method is kept and pinned in `tests/architecture/test_store_methods_have_production_callers.py` with this reason, so the choice is visible: either the note tier gains a minting path, or the registry goes too.

A deployed `config.toml` still carrying `[language]` or `[facts]` will REFUSE TO START — `Config` is `extra="forbid"`. Both sections must be deleted from the running deployment's config.toml before this image is deployed.

The participation eval suite drops from 15 cases to 11: the `fact-lookup` and `correction` knowledge-cut twin pairs were grounded in the fact tier, and a twin pair with no grounding to cut cannot flip.

No `[dreamer.budgets.*]` block ships any more — the five that existed were the two tiers' — so every surviving adaptor runs on `DreamBudgetConfig`'s defaults. That was already true for the note tier's three; it is now true for all of them, and `tests/test_config.py` asserts the empty section rather than leaving it to be inferred.
